purpose: Hold one chat's log, route human bursts and agent mail to member AgentDOs, and deliver system wakes (reminders, routines, initiative, unblocked tasks) under per-user and per-room budgets, each delivery deduplicated by a stable id.
summary: The core design holds: every delivery has a stable id and the inbox dedupes on it, human messages outrank agents, and burst pacing is simple and correct. Two narrow gaps need fixing: the daily turn charge is not idempotent on retry, and a refused human burst is dropped without a notice. The delivery receive-and-mark step is copied four times with diverging refusal policies, which is how the drop happened.

subareas.name: burst pacing
subareas.why: Debounce with an 8 s cap, fragment and typing extensions, and an idempotent INSERT OR IGNORE keyed by message id. Small and it does what the pacing rule asks.

subareas.name: human burst flush
subareas.why: takeTurn is charged per call and is not keyed by burst id, so a retry after a failure charges the user's daily quota again. A refused human envelope is logged and then marked delivered, so the message vanishes with no notice to the human.

subareas.name: agent mail
subareas.why: Hop, root, and stop limits and per-recipient queue rows work, and retries are safe because the inbox dedupes on agent:<msg>:<to>. Carries 8 ad hoc ALTER migrations and a re-queue on retried sends that is harmless but wasteful.

subareas.name: system wakes
subareas.why: Budget reserve, refund on refusal, id-keyed takeAutonomous, and a held outbox all work. Three near-identical follow, wake, unfollow blocks, and HeldWakes.due ignores its now argument.

subareas.name: coordination state (asks, team, reports, signals, routines)
subareas.why: Partially read. Reports.sendResults stamps openedAt with Date.now() per attempt, which is not a stable id, but its held batches carry only routine_result signals today. Prune logic is three different styles.

subareas.name: RoomDO shell and log
subareas.why: log.addMessage is idempotent by clientId or run. adopt() checks the DO name against room:<user>:<room>. About 60 methods, most one-line RPC delegations. Migrations run in two places. Only partially read: members, workspace, memory, pending, proposals, chief, rich-text.

strengths: Every delivery has a stable id and the inbox dedupes on it (core/agent/src/inbox.ts:48-52): human:<msg>, agent:<msg>:<to>, reminder:, routine:, initiative:, unblocked:. Retrying a partial burst is safe.

Human outranks agents: inbox PRIORITY by sender kind, mail to a burst-addressed agent is held until the burst is delivered (mail-drain.ts burstAddressed and drain), and initiative or reminder wakes return busy while a human is here (wake-delivery.ts:50, 75-80).
No waits on another DO inside AgentDO.receive. RoomDO awaits receive only from alarm or burst paths, and fire-and-forget calls use waitUntil.
Autonomous budget is id-keyed in UserDO (user/user-do.ts:491-496) and refunded on refusal (wake-delivery.ts deliverWake). Room-side reserve and refund match.
Burst cap by envelope bytes and count (burst.ts deliverable) keeps a backlog from exceeding the inbox entry size in one call.

problems.title: Daily turn charge is not idempotent on retry
problems.evidence: burst-flush.ts:71-73 calls userStub.takeTurn() on every attempt until setMeta('turn_taken') at line 85. user/user-do.ts:532-538 takeTurn() has no id, so each call increments the day's count. Compare takeAutonomous(id) at user-do.ts:496, which is keyed. If chat() rejects after takeTurn() succeeds (Promise.all at line 73), flush's catch retries and charges a second turn.
problems.fix: Pass burstId into UserDO.takeTurn and key the day count by id, as takeAutonomous does, or write the turn_taken marker before the chat call.

problems.title: A refused human burst is silently dropped
problems.evidence: burst-flush.ts:101-104 logs a non-full refusal and continues. burst.delivered(envelopes) at line 112 runs regardless, so the human message leaves pending with no notice. Refusal comes from inbox.ts:74 (too_large), which checks envelope plus brief against 128 KB. burst.ts MAX_DELIVERY_BYTES caps only the raw envelope at 64 KB, before withContext adds the quote and attachment lines and before the brief is counted.
problems.fix: Give a refused human envelope the same treatment mail gets (mail-drain.ts refused()): post a system notice to the human, then drop it. Or count the brief in deliverable().

problems.title: The receive-and-mark step is copied four times with diverging refusal policies
problems.evidence: burst-flush.ts:99-107 (drops silently), mail-drain.ts:138-149 (notifies the sender), room-do.ts:146-155 (drops, no retry), wake-delivery.ts deliverWake (refunds, marks, returns refused). Each does receive, refused check, mail.delivered, markReactionsBriefed.
problems.fix: One deliverTo(member, envelopes, policy) in deliver.ts. Choose refusal behaviour once. Removes about 25 lines and the divergence that caused the drop above.

problems.title: endRun marks the run ended after awaits
problems.evidence: room-do.ts:860-875. bubbles.markEnded(runId) runs after captureAnswer and touchChat. touchChat is not caught. If it throws, a retry sees first === true and repeats the trace, answerAsks, and capture.
problems.fix: Mark ended before the awaits, or catch touchChat as touchSoon does.

problems.title: Retried agent sends re-queue mail
problems.evidence: mail-drain.ts:59 queue(slug, out.send) runs even when out.fresh is false, so a retry of an already-sent message adds queue rows again. Safe only because the inbox dedupes on agent:<msg>:<to>.

problems.title: Held-signal batch id is a fresh timestamp
problems.evidence: reports.ts:89 signals({ openedAt: Date.now() }). UserDO.signals (user/user-do.ts:249) builds event:${openedAt} for event signals. Latent: sendResults only holds routine_result signals, which skip that branch.
problems.fix: Stamp the batch once when it is held, and reuse that value on retry.

problems.title: Memory capture for a human burst is best effort and not retried
problems.evidence: burst-flush.ts:124 captureHuman logs on failure, and the burst is already marked delivered.
problems.fix: Decide whether a lost capture matters. If yes, retry it from a pending row.

problems.title: HeldWakes.due ignores its time argument
problems.evidence: wake.ts:47-52 uses now only to prune. It returns the first N rows regardless of time, which retryHeld relies on, but the name says otherwise.
problems.fix: Rename the parameter, or drop it and document that every held row is due.

overengineering.title: Four copies of the deliver step
overengineering.why: The copies already diverged (burst drops, mail notifies), and the divergence is a live bug.

overengineering.title: Two migration mechanisms in one DO
overengineering.evidence: schema.ts MIGRATIONS with schema_version, plus PRAGMA table_info ALTERs in mail.ts:33-70 and asks.ts:12-14, and inbox in core/agent/src/inbox.ts
overengineering.why: Two ways to add a column. Fold the ad hoc ones into the versioned list the next time one of these tables changes.

overengineering.title: Three follow/wake/unfollow blocks
overengineering.why: Same try/catch and unfollow-on-not-delivered shape three times. A helper would do.

overengineering.title: Three prune strategies
overengineering.evidence: Math.random() < 0.02 in deliver.ts:73 and asks.ts:27, an hourly meta timestamp in mail.ts prune, none for the held outbox
overengineering.why: Not causing harm today, but one helper would be clearer.

overengineering.title: Dev RPC surface on the production RoomDO
overengineering.evidence: room-do.ts devSeed..devAgentMessage (about 25 lines) plus room/dev.ts (76 lines), guarded at runtime by NODE_ENV
overengineering.why: The verify suites need it. Keep it, but do not add more dev methods to the class.

overengineering.title: Burst fragment word list
overengineering.why: This is the human-pacing feature. The list is cheap and it has no unit test (see tests).

overengineering.title: Dead exports
overengineering.evidence: Checked every export in room/*.ts for callers in apps, core, and cli. Every apparent orphan (Unanswered, defaultTarget, safeName, attachmentPath, Compress, Rollup, Workspace, Holder) is used inside its own file.
overengineering.why: No DELETE candidates in this area.

tests: Unit: recipients.test.ts covers route() and buildBrief. reminders.test.ts covers reminder dedupe. initiative-runs.test.ts, initiative-safety.test.ts, and log-memory.test.ts cover wakes, budget, and log idempotency. limits.test.ts covers only the turn cap, not checkSend hop or root limits. workspace.test.ts covers tasks. Not unit-tested: burst debounce, isFragment, deliverable, takeTurn idempotency, the too_large refusal path, mail queue retry, held-wake retry. CLI: burst-backlog.ts sends 250 messages and checks each is heard once (the only end-to-end burst check), team-flow.ts and limits.ts cover agent mail and limits end to end. Gap: nothing forces a refused human burst or a retried turn charge. Those need a test that fails on the current code.
